pk/math.text: Child rote counts from 1 to 30.
Child counts up to 10 objects with one-to-one correspondence.
Child counts up to 10 items and demonstrates cardinality by communicating that the last number indicates how many items are in the set.
Child instantly recognizes the quantity of up to 6 objects without counting (subitizes).
Child recognizes numerals 0-10.
Child represents quantities up to 10.
Child begins to understand that numbers 0-10 can be composed and decomposed in various ways to represent a quantity.
Child compares sets of objects up to 10 using comparative language (e.g., greater/more than, less/fewer than, equal to/same number of).
Child uses objects, pictorial models, and/or a verbal word problem to represent adding up to 5 objects.
Child uses objects, pictorial models, and/or a verbal word problem to represent subtracting objects from a set of 5.
Child names and describes common 2D shapes and names at least 1 solid 3D shape.
Child creates shapes using materials and/or manipulatives.
Child demonstrates use of position words.
Child recognizes common shapes, regardless of orientation and size.
Child recognizes and compares heights or lengths of people or objects.
Child recognizes and compares capacity based on how much space exists within an object.
Child recognizes and compares weights of objects.
Child uses language to describe concepts associated with the passing of time within a day.
Child sorts objects that are the same and different into groups and uses language to describe how the groups are similar and different.
Child collects data and organizes it in a graphic representation.
Child recognizes, duplicates, extends, and creates patterns.

pk/language.text: Child shows understanding by responding appropriately to what has been communicated by adults and peers.
Child shows understanding by following three‐step verbal directions.
Child uses language for multiple purposes.
Child engages in conversations in appropriate ways, demonstrating knowledge of verbal and nonverbal conversational rules.
Child provides appropriate information in various situations.
Child matches language to social contexts.
Child’s speech is understood by both familiar and unfamiliar adults and peers.
Child demonstrates growing understanding of the intonation of language.
Child understands (receptive) and uses (expressive) a wide variety of words to label, describe and make connections among objects, people, places, actions, and events.
Child understands (receptive) and uses (expressive) the instructional language of the classroom.
Child consistently understands (receptive) and uses (expressive) new vocabulary acquired through books, conversations, and play.
Child typically uses complete sentences of four or more words with age- appropriate grammatical complexity, usually in standard word order.
Child correctly uses regular and irregular plurals, regular past tense, personal and possessive pronouns, and subject‐verb agreement.
Child uses sentences that combine multiple phrases or ideas.
Child uses sentences that provide many details, remains on topic, and clearly communicates intended meaning.
Child engages in story-related pre‐reading activities.
Child self‐selects books and other written materials to engage in pre‐reading behaviors.
Child recognizes that all print carries meaning and serves as a means for communication.
Child identifies the individual words in a spoken sentence.
Child distinguishes differences between similar-sounding words.
Child uses two familiar base words to form a compound word with pictorial or gestural supports.
Child manipulates compound words with pictorial or gestural support.
Child begins to blend and segment syllables in multisyllabic words.
Child identifies rhyming words.
Child identifies alliterative words with pictorial support.
Child identifies a familiar one-syllable word that is segmented by onset and rime (in English only).
Child blends and segments one-syllable words by phonemes with visual or gestural support.
Child recognizes and names at least 20 letters (upper- or lower-case letters).
Child recognizes at least 20 distinct letter-sound correspondences.
Child produces at least 20 distinct letter-sound correspondences.
Child retells or re‐enacts a story with a clear beginning, middle, and end.
Child uses information learned from books by describing, relating, categorizing, or comparing and contrasting.
Child asks and responds to questions relevant to the text read aloud.
Child makes inferences and predictions about a text.
Child can distinguish between elements of print including letters, words, and pictures.

Child holds books right side up and demonstrates understanding of print directionality (e.g., knows where a book starts and ends, turns pages, points to words left to right, top to bottom, with correct sweeping).
Child can identify some conventional features of print that communicate meaning including end punctuation and case.

pk/science.text: Child observes, investigates, describes, and discusses characteristics of common objects.
Child observes, investigates, describes, and discusses position and motion of objects.
Child uses simple scientific tools to learn about objects.
Child observes, investigates, describes, and discusses sources of energy including light, heat, and electricity.
Child observes, investigates, describes, and discusses the characteristics of organisms.
Child observes, describes, and discusses the life cycles of organisms.
Child observes, investigates, describes, and discusses the relationship of organisms in their environments.
Child observes, investigates, describes, and discusses earth materials, and their properties and uses.
Child identifies, observes, describes, and discusses objects in the sky.
Child observes and describes what happens during changes in the earth and sky.
Child demonstrates an understanding of the importance of caring for our environment and our planet.
Child demonstrates coordination and balance in isolation.
Child coordinates sequence of movements to perform tasks.
Child shows control of tasks that require small-muscle strength and control.
Child shows increasing control of tasks that require eye-hand coordination.
Child practices good habits of personal safety.
Child practices good habits of personal health and hygiene.
Child identifies good habits of nutrition and exercise.

pk/social.text: Child is aware of where own body is in space and respects personal boundaries.
Child shows self-awareness of physical attributes, personal preferences, and own abilities.
Child shows reasonable opinion of his own abilities and limitations.
Child shows initiative in trying new activities and demonstrates perseverance when attempting to overcome obstacles or challenges.
Child follows classroom rules and routines with occasional reminders from adults.
Child takes care of and manages classroom materials.
Child regulates own behavior with occasional reminders or assistance from adults.
Child begins to understand the connection between emotions and behaviors.
Child uses verbal and nonverbal communication to communicate basic emotions and feelings.
Child is able to manage intensity of emotions more consistently, although adult guidance is sometimes necessary.
Child sustains attention to personally chosen or routine (teacher-directed) tasks until completed.
Child remains focused on engaging, teacher-led group activities for up to 20 minutes.
Child uses effective verbal and nonverbal communication skills to build relationships with adults and peers.
Child assumes various roles and responsibilities as part of the classroom community.
Child shows competence in initiating social interactions.
Child increasingly interacts with peers during cooperative play scenarios that share a common plan and goal.
Child initiates problem‐solving strategies when experiencing conflicts with others and seeks adult support when necessary.
Child demonstrates empathy and caring for others.
Child interacts with peers and has preferred friends.
Child demonstrates an understanding that others have perspectives and feelings that are similar and/or different from her own.

Child identifies similarities and differences between himself, classmates, and other people through specific characteristics and cultural influences.
Child identifies similarities and differences in characteristics of families.
Child connects his life to events, time, and routines.
Child demonstrates an understanding that all people need food, clothing, and shelter.
Child demonstrates an understanding of what it means to be a consumer.
Child discusses the roles and responsibilities of family, school, and community helpers.
Child identifies and creates common geographic features.
Child explores geography tools and resources.
Child identifies the United States and Texas flag.
Child recites the Pledge of Allegiance to the United States flag and the Texas flag and observes a moment of silence.
The child engages in voting as a method for group decision‐making.
